# GitHub Issue #368

## Title
A JSON-encoded string in params reaches a string input still encoded

## Description
## What happened

In cv/pi-action#76, the model sent a PR body to a program with a string input, `async ({ shell: { execFile } }, body: string) => …`. In `params` it sent the body as a JSON string literal: quotes, and `\n` escapes for the line breaks. `resolveToolInput` (`src/tool/input.ts`) decodes only a JSON object or array, and only when the program's input cannot be a string. So the program got the encoded text, and `gh pr create --body` posted it as is: a body that starts with `"` and shows `\n` instead of line breaks.

The run: https://github.com/cv/pi-action/actions/runs/43522489097 (pit v0.36.2).

## Proposed fix

Decode a `params` string that is a JSON string literal, for any declared input. Leave a quoted string that is not valid JSON unchanged. A program that really wants a value with literal quotes around it would get it decoded; that seems rare.

This patch applies to `main`, and `test/tool/input.test.ts` passes (19 tests):

```diff
diff --git a/src/tool/input.ts b/src/tool/input.ts
--- a/src/tool/input.ts
+++ b/src/tool/input.ts
@@ -3,11 +3,22 @@ import { programInputAdmitsString } from "../functions/source.js";
 /**
  * Some clients deliver the `params` tool argument as a JSON string. Decode a string that holds a
  * JSON object or array when the program's declared input cannot accept a string; otherwise pass
- * the value through unchanged so validation reports any mismatch against the declared type.
+ * the value through unchanged so validation reports any mismatch against the declared type. A
+ * string that is itself a JSON string literal ("line\\nline") is decoded for every input.
  */
 export function resolveToolInput(source: string, params: unknown): unknown {
-  if (typeof params !== "string" || programInputAdmitsString(source) !== false) return params;
+  if (typeof params !== "string") return params;
   const text = params.trim();
+  // A string sent JSON-encoded, quotes and \n escapes included, is never meant literally.
+  if (text.length >= 2 && text.startsWith('"') && text.endsWith('"')) {
+    try {
+      const decoded = JSON.parse(text) as unknown;
+      if (typeof decoded === "string") return decoded;
+    } catch {
+      // Not a JSON string: keep it.
+    }
+  }
+  if (programInputAdmitsString(source) !== false) return params;
   if (!(text.startsWith("{") || text.startsWith("["))) return params;
diff --git a/test/tool/input.test.ts b/test/tool/input.test.ts
--- a/test/tool/input.test.ts
+++ b/test/tool/input.test.ts
@@ -102,6 +102,18 @@ describe("resolveToolInput", () => {
       params: "42",
       expected: "42",
     },
+    {
+      name: "a JSON-encoded string for a string input",
+      source: "async ({}, body: string) => body",
+      params: JSON.stringify("Title\n\n## Section"),
+      expected: "Title\n\n## Section",
+    },
+    {
+      name: "a quoted string that is not JSON",
+      source: "async ({}, body: string) => body",
+      params: '"a\\q"',
+      expected: '"a\\q"',
+    },
     {
       name: "an already decoded object",
```

Reported from cv/pi-action#76.


## Task
let's ship this as a new patch release

## Your Reply

pi-action posts your final response as a comment on this issue or pull request. **Do not post your reply yourself**, for example with `gh issue comment`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr review`, or `gh api`. That would post the same answer twice. Use `gh` to comment only where the task asks for it, such as on another issue.

## Important: Artifact and Script Requirements

**CRITICAL:** After the GitHub Action finishes running, all files modified or created are lost, and the GitHub Action runner is destroyed. Therefore:

1. **All generated code and artifacts MUST be committed** - Any files you create, modify, or generate must be committed and pushed to the repository before the action completes. Nothing will persist otherwise.

2. **Any throw-away scripts generated MUST be run immediately** - If you create temporary scripts (like `/tmp/create-issues.sh` or similar), you must execute them during the same session. They will be lost when the runner terminates.

3. **Commit and push all work** - Always end your work by committing and pushing changes to ensure they persist beyond the GitHub Action execution.
